headline: Travis County Power Backup Report
summary: Homes in Travis County face an elevated risk. A long outage of 12 hours or more happens about once every 10 years. This comes from 8 years of records since 2018. In February 2021, 43% of homes in the county lost power. The longest-waiting tenth waited about 96 hours. In February 2023, 29% of homes in the county lost power. The longest-waiting tenth waited about 132 hours. One Core lasts about 18 hours in August. One Core lasts about 35 hours in March. Two Cores last about 37 hours in August. Two Cores cover 74% of past 12-hour-plus outage hours. Base confirms sizing at install.
